title: Unit-normalized full and bounded-below derived functors of an additive functor
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with ordinary derived localizations $Q_{\mathcal A},Q_{\mathcal B}$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume $\mathcal A$ has enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and every cochain complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex, meaning a complex $I$ such that every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $F_K$ its degreewise functor on complexes modulo chain homotopy. Then $Q_{\mathcal B}F_K$ has a total right derived pair $(RF,\eta)$ as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. For any quasi-isomorphism $s:C\to I$ with $I$ K-injective, $\eta_I$ is invertible and the canonical value isomorphism is
$$RF(Q_{\mathcal A}C)\xrightarrow{RF(Q_{\mathcal A}s)}RF(Q_{\mathcal A}I)\xrightarrow{\eta_I^{-1}}Q_{\mathcal B}(FI).$$
Let $(R^+F,\alpha)$ be the bounded-below right derived pair [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective], and let $\iota_{\mathcal A},\iota_{\mathcal B}$ denote the full inclusions of the bounded-below categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\theta:RF\,\iota_{\mathcal A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\iota_{\mathcal B}R^+F$$
satisfying $\theta_{Q^+C}\eta_C=\iota_{\mathcal B}(\alpha_C)$ for every bounded-below complex $C$, with the canonical localization identifications understood. In particular $RF$ carries $D^+(\mathcal A)$ into $D^+(\mathcal B)$. For every bounded-below degreewise injective complex $J$, both units are invertible and $\theta_{Q^+J}=\iota_{\mathcal B}(\alpha_J)\eta_J^{-1}$; both derived values are computed by $FJ$. For every bounded-below injective resolution $s:C\to J$, the same components satisfy
$$\theta_{Q^+C}=\iota_{\mathcal B}(R^+F(Q^+s))^{-1}\,\iota_{\mathcal B}(\alpha_J)\,\eta_J^{-1}\,RF(Q_{\mathcal A}s).$$
These formulas are independent of the injective representatives and natural for all derived morphisms. No left exactness of $F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tags 070K (lemma-enough-K-injectives-implies), 070I (lemma-K-injective), 070J (lemma-bounded-below-injectives-K-injective), 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist); unit-normalized comparison of these constructions, extracted from returned item steps 3-5.

proof.text: Use the universal property and K-injective unit invertibility of the recorded pair (RF, eta). Localization inverts any quasi-isomorphism s, so RF(Qh(s)) followed by eta_I inverse is invertible.

For every bounded below degreewise injective complex J, bounded-below injectivity makes J K-injective. Thus eta_J is invertible. Let U be the restriction of RF to D+(A), and let eta+ be the restriction of eta. Mathlib HomotopyCategory.Plus.localizerMorphism_derives and LocalizerMorphism.Derives.isRightDerivedFunctor_of_isIso identify (U, eta+) as a right derived pair: the criterion tests exactly these invertible components on the injective derivability structure. This is the existing injective-resolution proof of bounded-below derivability, applied with target D(B). The underlying mathematical justification is the injective-resolution comparison of Tags 05TI and 05TH: every bounded below complex admits a quasi-isomorphism to an injective one, and the localization on injective complexes computes all derived maps. Mathlib packages precisely this criterion, not a new hypothesis.

Put V = Rplus followed by the inclusion D+(B) -> D(B), with alpha+ obtained by whiskering alpha. The bounded-below derived unit alpha_J is invertible on degreewise injectives, and its included image is invertible. Apply the same Mathlib injective derivability criterion to obtain a right derived pair (V, alpha+). Functor.rightDerivedUnique now supplies theta : U isomorphic to V. Its rightDerivedNatTrans_app equation gives eta_C followed by theta_(Q+C) = inclusion(alpha_C) on every bounded-below complex C. The rightDerived_ext uniqueness theorem shows that every other unit-normalized comparison equals theta.

The value V(X) lies in D+(B). Transport this property across theta_X inverse using closure under isomorphisms. On an injective J, cancel eta_J in the unit equation to get theta_(Q+J) = eta_J inverse followed by inclusion(alpha_J).

For a bounded-below quasi-isomorphism s:C -> J, localization inverts Q+(s), hence V(Q+(s)) is invertible. Naturality of theta says theta_C followed by V(Q+(s)) = U(Q+(s)) followed by theta_J. Cancel V(Q+(s)) and substitute the injective formula. The same calculation for any isomorphism q:X -> Q+(J) yields the representative formula, using q inverse instead of the inverse image of s. This proves both formulas for every resolution and representative without choosing either.

For the full-category formula, naturality of eta at f:I -> J gives eta_I inverse followed by Qh(F(f)) = RF(Qh(f)) followed by eta_J inverse. Precompose by RF(Qh(s)), use functoriality and the assumed equation Qh(s) followed by Qh(f) = u followed by Qh(t), then reassociate. This proves the stated equality for every derived u and every f with that equation; no lift needs to be chosen.

proof_origin.place: Tags 070K, 070J, 05TI and 05TH; Lean implementation uses Mathlib injective derivability (DerivabilityStructureInjectives.lean, localizerMorphism_derives; Derives.lean, isRightDerivedFunctor_of_isIso) and rightDerivedUnique/rightDerived_ext. The two units are tested on injectives and compared by their universal properties; all value formulas are naturality and cancellation.
